title: The numbers
heading: The full picture,
intro: National screening participation, broken down a few different ways. Numbers describe the system, not any one person's choices.

participation.label: National participation
participation.description: of eligible people aged 25–74 had an HPV screening test in the latest reporting period.

chart.title: Screening participation rate
chart.ariaLabel: Participation trend across three overlapping reporting periods
chart.caption: In {{window}}, {{percent}}% of eligible people aged 25–74 had a screening test. This changed from {{firstPercent}}% in {{firstWindow}} ({{change}} percentage points).
chart.captionState: In {{window}}, {{percent}}% of eligible people aged 25–74 in {{place}} had a screening test. This changed from {{firstPercent}}% in {{firstWindow}} ({{change}} percentage points).
chart.axisNote: The scale starts at {{min}}% so changes are easier to see.
chart.caveatWindows: Each period counts tests over 5.5 years, so periods overlap. They show a trend, not separate years.
chart.caveatStates: AIHW advises against directly comparing states and territories, because their populations, geography and policies differ.

ageGroups.label: By age group
ageGroups.title: Participation varies by age.
ageGroups.note: Differences between groups can reflect access to services, language support, and how familiar the system feels — not personal choice.
ageGroups.caption: In {{window}}, participation ranged from {{lowestPercent}}% (ages {{lowestAge}}) to {{highestPercent}}% (ages {{highestAge}}).
ageGroups.quote: Participants aged 70–74 have re-entered the target age group under the renewed NCSP after leaving the previous NCSP after age 69, so lower participation is expected in this age group.
ageGroups.quoteSource: AIHW, National Cervical Screening Program monitoring report 2025

selfCollection.label: Self-collection
selfCollection.title: Self-collected HPV tests, by month
selfCollection.description: HPV screening tests were self-collected in {{year}}, about {{share}}% of all HPV tests.
selfCollection.caption: Up from {{firstCount}} self-collected tests in {{firstYear}}.
selfCollection.accuracy: A self-collected cervical screening test is just as safe and accurate at detecting HPV as a clinician-collected sample.
selfCollection.caveatTests: These are counts of tests, not people.

socioeconomic.label: By area
socioeconomic.title: Participation by area disadvantage
socioeconomic.caption: In {{window}}, participation was {{q1Percent}}% in the areas with the most disadvantage and {{q5Percent}}% in the areas with the least disadvantage.
socioeconomic.caveatArea: These are area-level patterns. They describe areas, not individual people, and say nothing about how any one person, or people of any background, choose to screen.
socioeconomic.caveatStructural: Differences between areas reflect things like access to services, cost and time, not individual choices.
socioeconomic.quote: People experiencing socio-economic disadvantage can face extra barriers to screening, such as out-of-pocket costs and competing priorities like work.
socioeconomic.quoteSource: Summarised from health.gov.au, NCSP Healthcare Provider Toolkit

sources.title: Where the data comes from
sources.description: Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW), National Cervical Screening Program monitoring report 2025; Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), Census of Population and Housing 2021 (local area map). Figures are updated as new reporting becomes available.
